newsitem.title: THAILAND: PTTEP 1996 net profit rises 13 percent.
newsitem.headline: PTTEP 1996 net profit rises 13 percent.

text.p: The exploration arm of state-run Petroleum Authority of Thailand, PTT Exploration and Production Plc, said on Wednesday that its 1996 net profit rose 13 percent to 1.079 billion baht.
The firm said its total revenue rose 35 pct to 6.095 billion baht in 1996 and earnings per share was 3.48 baht versus 3.09 in 1995.

It attributed the rise in revenue to increased production from the Bongkot field in the Gulf of Thailand and the sales of natural gas which rose sharply to 350 mmcfd (million cubic feet per day) in the second quarter of 1996 from 250 mmcfd before that.
An increase in 1996 oil and natural gas prices compared to those in 1995 also helped, the company added.
Production by PTTEP and it subidiaries in 1996 amounted to 14 million barrels of oil equivalent, up 31 percent from 1995.
The company had recorded reserves of 502 mmvoe (barrels of oil equivalent) in 1996, up three percent from 1995.
